meta.bit_reading_note: circuits A and B have sixteen classical bits, qubit QUBITS[i] (the label's qubits, in order) into clbit i (the label's clbit_of_qubit); the circuits on M alone (M-zero, M-one, Z) have one, M into c0
meta.description: Kickoff 61, the readout check on ibm_fez: on the sixteen distinct qubits of Kickoff 54's six chains, fixed by the rule (29, 30, 31, 73, 74, 75, 96, 103, 104, 116, 120, 121, 142, 143, 144 and 145), A measures all sixteen with no gate and B puts one X on each, then the same measures; on each waiting qubit M (30, 74, 121, 103, 144, 143) alone, M-zero (measure, no gate), M-one (X, then measure) and Z (H, H, measure). 20 circuits, each 2 copies of 2000 shots, 40 positions in one random order; the sampler's own dynamical decoupling and twirling off and no readout error mitigation, as IBM recorded them.
meta.bit_order: Qiskit bitstrings, rightmost character = classical bit 0

built_from.how: outside the package (hw_61.py, source_code): A, B, M-zero, M-one and Z, translated by manacitra.wait.to_backend (optimization level 0, the named qubits as the layout) and scheduled by manacitra.wait.scheduled, against the live ibm_fez target at build (dt 4 ns)

superseded.closing_comment: Superseded by version 2 (issue #43 ) before the run: the qubit count was wrong (eighteen written where the six chains hold sixteen distinct qubits). No job ran under this version. The file stays published as k61-rule-v1-superseded.md.
superseded.what: version 1 counted the six fixed chains' qubits as eighteen; they hold sixteen distinct qubits (143 and 144 are in two chains each). The runner's check against the rule found it before anything was built, read through the account or submitted; version 2 corrects the count and changes nothing else in the design

fixed_before_the_data.rule: per qubit, e = (P(1|0) + P(0|1)) / 2 from A and B, the copies pooled; p, the published readout error at the stamp in force at submission, and at every distinct stamp dated after it and no later than the job's finish; CONSISTENT if e's 90% interval meets [p - tol, p + tol], tol the larger of 0.02 and p/2; INCONSISTENT otherwise. H61: PUBLISHED READABLE if every qubit is CONSISTENT; PUBLISHED NOT READABLE if six or more of the sixteen are INCONSISTENT; MIXED otherwise
fixed_before_the_data.bootstraps: one bootstrap, seed bootstrap, n_boot draws, in the order analyse_61.py fixes: A, then B (the two copies drawn with replacement, each redrawn from a multinomial over its whole sixteen-bit outcomes, so the sixteen qubits are drawn jointly), then per M in the rule's order (30, 74, 121, 103, 144, 143) M-zero, M-one and Z (the copies with replacement, each redrawn binomially)

"""Kickoff 61 analysis, fixed before the data (kickoff section 3; k61-rule.md, version 2).

From the counts of the 40 positions (20 circuits, 2 copies each, 2,000 shots each):
- Per qubit q of the sixteen (clbit i of circuits A and B holds QUBITS[i]): P(1|0) = the fraction of A's shots with
  q's bit 1, P(0|1) = the fraction of B's shots with q's bit 0, the copies pooled; the measured readout error
  e = (P(1|0) + P(0|1)) / 2, the average IBM's published readout_error is defined as.
- The published readout error p per qubit: the value at the stamp in force at submission; if a new stamp appears before
  the job finishes (a distinct stamp in stamps-61.csv dated after the submission stamp and no later than the job's
  finish time in IBM's record), the comparison is also made against each such stamp, and all are recorded.
- 90% intervals (5th and 95th percentiles, the repository's tests/_reuse_runs.pct) from one bootstrap, seed 61, 10,000
  draws, in a fixed order: circuit A, then circuit B (for each, the two copies drawn with replacement, each redrawn
  from a multinomial over its whole 16-bit outcomes, so the sixteen qubits are drawn jointly), then per M in the
  rule's order (30, 74, 121, 103, 144, 143) M-zero, M-one and Z (the copies with replacement, each redrawn binomially).
- Per qubit: CONSISTENT if e's interval contains a value within the larger of 0.02 and p/2 of p (the interval
  [lo, hi] meets [p - tol, p + tol]); INCONSISTENT otherwise.
- H61: PUBLISHED READABLE if every qubit is CONSISTENT; PUBLISHED NOT READABLE if six or more of the sixteen are
  INCONSISTENT; MIXED otherwise.
Beside the verdict, not used in it: (1) whether every one of the sixteen has measured e below 0.05; (2) per M, P(1|0)
and P(0|1) alone (M-zero, M-one) beside the values from A and B; (3) the zero-wait baseline P(1) per M (Z) and whether
any exceeds 0.1; (4) the calibration record: every stamp read, the job's status changes, and the sixteen qubits'
published readout error at every stamp read.

Usage: python analyse_61.py                 (Kickoff 61's files; writes results-61.json)
       python analyse_61.py --synthetic     (counts built to give CONSISTENT on every qubit, INCONSISTENT on eight,
                                             and, beside, INCONSISTENT on three; on the dry run's labels)"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import hashlib
import json
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "site"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "src-e45f15d" / "tests"))
import _reuse_runs as reuse  # noqa: E402  the repository's percentile helper

pct = reuse.pct
QUBITS = [29, 30, 31, 73, 74, 75, 96, 103, 104, 116, 120, 121, 142, 143, 144, 145]
MS = [30, 74, 121, 103, 144, 143]
SEED, N_BOOT, CHUNK = 61, 10_000, 1_000
FLOOR, NOT_READABLE_AT = 0.02, 6
LOW_E, Z_HIGH = 0.05, 0.1


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def tol(p):
    return max(FLOOR, p / 2)


def verdict_q(ci, p):
    lo, hi = ci
    return "CONSISTENT" if (lo <= p + tol(p) and hi >= p - tol(p)) else "INCONSISTENT"


def h61(verdicts):
    n_in = sum(v == "INCONSISTENT" for v in verdicts.values())
    if n_in == 0:
        return "PUBLISHED READABLE", n_in
    if n_in >= NOT_READABLE_AT:
        return "PUBLISHED NOT READABLE", n_in
    return "MIXED", n_in


def gather(labels, counts):
    """Per circuit key: the copies in order, each (copy, {outcome: n})."""
    out = {}
    for lab, cts in zip(labels, counts):
        key = (lab["circuit"], lab["M"])
        out.setdefault(key, []).append((lab["copy"], {k.replace(" ", ""): int(n) for k, n in cts.items()}))
    for k in out:
        out[k].sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    return out


def bits_matrix(keys, n):
    """Outcome strings (Qiskit order, clbit 0 rightmost) as a (len(keys), n) 0/1 matrix, column i = clbit i."""
    return np.array([[int(k[::-1][i]) for i in range(n)] for k in keys], dtype=np.int64)


def analyse(labels, counts, published_by_stamp, rng_seed=SEED):
    """published_by_stamp: {label: {"stamp_utc": ..., "readout_error": {str(q): p}}}, in the order to report; the first
    is the stamp in force at submission."""
    g = gather(labels, counts)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(rng_seed)
    n = len(QUBITS)

    def joint(key, flip):
        """Pooled per-qubit fraction of the target outcome (1 for A, 0 for B) and its bootstrap draws."""
        copies = g[key]
        keys = sorted({k for _, d in copies for k in d})
        B = bits_matrix(keys, n)
        if flip:
            B = 1 - B
        V = np.array([[d.get(k, 0) for k in keys] for _, d in copies], float)
        tot = V.sum(1)
        point = (V.sum(0) @ B) / tot.sum()
        freq = V / tot[:, None]
        draws = np.zeros((N_BOOT, n))
        idx = rng.integers(0, V.shape[0], size=(N_BOOT, V.shape[0]))
        for s in range(0, N_BOOT, CHUNK):
            acc, accn = np.zeros((min(CHUNK, N_BOOT - s), n)), np.zeros(min(CHUNK, N_BOOT - s))
            for j in range(V.shape[0]):
                pick = idx[s:s + CHUNK, j]
                m = rng.multinomial(tot[pick].astype(np.int64), freq[pick])
                acc += m @ B
                accn += tot[pick]
            draws[s:s + CHUNK] = acc / accn[:, None]
        return point, draws

    def single(key, target):
        """Pooled fraction of the target outcome on clbit 0 and its bootstrap draws (copies with replacement, binomial)."""
        copies = g[key]
        o = np.array([sum(v for k, v in d.items() if k[-1] == str(target)) for _, d in copies])
        t = np.array([sum(d.values()) for _, d in copies])
        acc1, accn = np.zeros(N_BOOT), np.zeros(N_BOOT)
        for _ in range(len(o)):
            pick = rng.integers(0, len(o), size=N_BOOT)
            acc1 += rng.binomial(t[pick], o[pick] / t[pick])
            accn += t[pick]
        return float(o.sum() / t.sum()), acc1 / accn

    p10, p10b = joint(("A", None), flip=False)
    p01, p01b = joint(("B", None), flip=True)
    e, eb = (p10 + p01) / 2, (p10b + p01b) / 2
    alone = {}
    for M in MS:
        a10, a10b = single(("M-zero", M), 1)
        a01, a01b = single(("M-one", M), 0)
        z1, z1b = single(("Z", M), 1)
        i = QUBITS.index(M)
        alone[str(M)] = {"alone": {"P10": a10, "P10_ci90": pct(a10b), "P01": a01, "P01_ci90": pct(a01b), "e": (a10 + a01) / 2, "e_ci90": pct((a10b + a01b) / 2)},
                         "together": {"P10": float(p10[i]), "P10_ci90": pct(p10b[:, i]), "P01": float(p01[i]), "P01_ci90": pct(p01b[:, i]),
                                      "e": float(e[i]), "e_ci90": pct(eb[:, i])},
                         "alone_minus_together": {"P10": a10 - float(p10[i]), "P10_ci90": pct(a10b - p10b[:, i]),
                                                  "P01": a01 - float(p01[i]), "P01_ci90": pct(a01b - p01b[:, i])},
                         "Z_P1": z1, "Z_P1_ci90": pct(z1b), "Z_above_0.1": z1 > Z_HIGH}
    per_q = {str(q): {"P10": float(p10[i]), "P10_ci90": pct(p10b[:, i]), "P01": float(p01[i]), "P01_ci90": pct(p01b[:, i]),
                      "e": float(e[i]), "e_ci90": pct(eb[:, i]), "e_below_0.05": bool(e[i] < LOW_E)} for i, q in enumerate(QUBITS)}
    comparisons = {}
    for lab, pub in published_by_stamp.items():
        v, rows = {}, {}
        for q in QUBITS:
            p = pub["readout_error"].get(str(q))
            if p is None:
                v[str(q)] = "INCONSISTENT"
                rows[str(q)] = {"p": None, "note": "no published value; counted INCONSISTENT"}
                continue
            ci = per_q[str(q)]["e_ci90"]
            v[str(q)] = verdict_q(ci, p)
            rows[str(q)] = {"p": p, "tolerance": tol(p), "accepted_range": [p - tol(p), p + tol(p)], "e": per_q[str(q)]["e"], "e_ci90": ci,
                            "e_minus_p": per_q[str(q)]["e"] - p, "verdict": v[str(q)]}
        H, n_in = h61(v)
        comparisons[lab] = {"stamp_utc": pub["stamp_utc"], "per_qubit": rows, "n_inconsistent": n_in,
                            "inconsistent": [q for q in v if v[q] == "INCONSISTENT"], "H61": H}
    return {"per_qubit": per_q, "comparisons": comparisons,
            "beside": {"all_e_below_0.05": all(r["e_below_0.05"] for r in per_q.values()),
                       "qubits_e_at_or_above_0.05": [q for q, r in per_q.items() if not r["e_below_0.05"]],
                       "alone_against_together": alone, "any_Z_above_0.1": any(a["Z_above_0.1"] for a in alone.values())}}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the run's files
def stamps_for_comparison(sub, res_counts):
    """The stamp in force at submission, then each distinct stamp dated after it and no later than the job's finish."""
    rows = list(csv.DictReader((HERE / "stamps-61.csv").open()))
    s0 = sub["stamp_row_at_submission"]["stamp_utc"]
    fin = (res_counts.get("timestamps") or {}).get("finished")
    fin_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(str(fin).replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone(timezone.utc) if fin else None
    f = lambda s: datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    by_stamp = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_stamp.setdefault(r["stamp_utc"], r)
    out = {"at submission": by_stamp[s0]}
    for st, r in sorted(by_stamp.items()):
        if f(st) > f(s0) and (fin_dt is None or f(st) <= fin_dt):
            out[f"new stamp {st}"] = r
    return {k: {"stamp_utc": r["stamp_utc"], "readout_error": json.loads(r["readout_error_16"])} for k, r in out.items()}, fin


def calibration_record():
    rows = list(csv.DictReader((HERE / "stamps-61.csv").open()))
    status, last = [], None
    for r in rows:
        if r["job_status"] and r["job_status"] != last:
            status.append({"utc": r["utc"], "status": r["job_status"]})
            last = r["job_status"]
    reads = [{"utc": r["utc"], "kind": r["kind"], "stamp_utc": r["stamp_utc"], "new_stamp": r["new_stamp"],
              "changed": {k: r[k] for k in ("q_T1", "q_T2", "q_readout_error", "g1_any", "cz_error", "cz_length", "other_values_changed") if r.get(k)},
              "readout_error_16": json.loads(r["readout_error_16"])} for r in rows]
    return {"reads": reads, "n_reads": len(rows), "distinct_stamps": sorted({r["stamp_utc"] for r in rows}), "job_status_changes_at_polls": status}
